top_findings.title: Strong metrics but limited generalization proof
top_findings.risk: The project may still fail on unseen textbooks, noisy notes, or uncommon question styles.

top_findings.title: Retrieval and synthesis services are too large
top_findings.risk: Future accuracy fixes can regress unrelated query categories.

top_findings.title: Advanced controls still leak into normal UX
top_findings.risk: Normal users may feel they are operating a RAG workbench instead of chatting with an academic assistant.

top_findings.title: Release manifest lags newer metrics
top_findings.risk: Public reviewers may see inconsistent reliability evidence.

top_findings.title: Human evaluation loop needs more real-user data
top_findings.risk: Automatic metrics may overstate perceived usefulness.

recommended_next_version: Expand unseen reviewed eval data to at least 100-150 natural queries.
Refactor answer planning, evidence ranking, context packing, citation verification, and fallback composition into smaller backend modules.
Move retrieval controls and thread IDs behind an explicit developer/debug mode.
Upgrade answer presentation to feel simpler, more explanatory, and more student-friendly.
Publish a new release manifest after the next verified ship gate.
Refresh screenshots and GIFs after the next UI pass.
release_position: Shippable as a local-first portfolio/demo MVP; not yet a commercial production-grade arbitrary-document system.
